name: Starr Campground
note: USFS Malheur NF (Blue Mountain RD), on US-395 ~16 mi south of John Day at ~5,150 ft in ponderosa pine. Two loops (~11-15 sites), upper loop mostly pull-throughs plus back-ins; vault toilets, no potable water. First-come, first-served (all Malheur NF camping is FCFS). No published RV length limit; pull-through sites fit a 23-ft rig. --Claude

name: Wickiup Campground (Malheur NF)
note: USFS Malheur NF (Blue Mountain RD), along Canyon Creek on Forest Road 15 (off County Rd 65), ~16 mi south of Canyon City. Small campground (~6 nonelectric sites; historically 9 trailer sites), vault toilet, no potable water, pack-in/pack-out, 14-day limit. First-come, first-served (all Malheur NF camping is FCFS). Maintained forest-road access; small/mid RVs. --Claude

name: Camp Comfort Campground
note: USFS Umpqua NF (Tiller RD) on the upper South Umpqua River among old-growth cedar/fir. 5 standard sites, max vehicle length 22 ft, no restrooms or potable water, first-come, first-served. NOTE: currently closed for danger-tree treatment (no reopening date posted) -- verify status before visiting. --Claude

name: Cover Campground
note: USFS Umpqua NF (Tiller RD) along Jackson Creek (South Umpqua tributary) on Forest Road 29, ~13 mi up Jackson Creek Rd. 7 primitive sites, max vehicle length 22 ft, no potable water, on-site fee tubes, first-come, first-served. NOTE: currently closed for danger-tree treatment (no reopening date posted) -- verify status before visiting. --Claude

name: Trout Creek Campground (Willamette NF)
note: USFS Willamette NF (Sweet Home RD) along the South Santiam River on Hwy 20, ~20 mi east of Sweet Home. 24 sites on a single loop with four RV pull-throughs 24-40 ft; both reservable and FCFS sites via recreation.gov. River wading/fishing plus the Trout Creek and Walton Ranch interpretive trails. --Claude

name: Yukwah Campground
note: USFS Willamette NF (Sweet Home RD) along the South Santiam River on Hwy 20, ~21 mi east of Sweet Home (just east of Trout Creek CG). 20 single sites accommodating trailers 18-32 ft depending on site; both reservable and FCFS via recreation.gov. Accessible Yukwah Nature Trail winds through the campground; fishing/swimming in the river. --Claude

name: Whitehorse Falls Campground
note: USFS Umpqua NF campground, 5 sites along the Clearwater River beside Whitehorse Falls (North Umpqua RD, ~66 mi E of Roseburg on Hwy 138). Vault toilets, no potable water, pack out trash; max vehicle length 25 ft. First-come, first-served (pay envelopes on site). --Claude

name: Sunset Cove Campground
note: Deschutes NF (Crescent RD) campground on the NE shore of Odell Lake, ~20 standard nonelectric sites in 3 loops, vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups; boat ramp with FCFS slips. Mix of reservable and first-come sites via recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Gold Lake Campground
note: Willamette NF (Middle Fork Ranger District) at Gold Lake, a fly-fishing/non-motorized lake near the Cascade crest; 21 sites, no hookups, first-come, first-served. Max trailer length 24 ft on a narrow access road, so a 23-ft rig fits with care. --Claude

name: Lava Flow Campground
note: Deschutes NF (Crescent Ranger District) on the east shore of Davis Lake below a large lava flow; 6 primitive sites for RV/trailer/tent, no drinking water, vault toilet, first-come, first-served. Max vehicle length 36 ft. Access road to the NE shore is closed in spring/early summer to protect wildlife. --Claude

name: Pioneer Ford Campground
note: Deschutes NF (Sisters RD) campground on the Metolius River ~23 mi north of Sisters; 20 sites (mix of back-in and pull-through), max site spur length 40 ft, vault toilets, no hookups. Reservable online, some sites FCFS. --Claude

name: Cove Creek Campground (Detroit Lake)
note: Willamette NF (Detroit RD) campground on the south shore of Detroit Lake - the largest NF campground on the lake. 63 sites (55 single + 6 double), no hookups but flush toilets, drinking water, coin showers, boat ramp + dock; trailers to 30 ft. Mix of reservable + FCFS. --Claude

name: Diamond Lake Campground
note: Umpqua NF campground on the east shore of Diamond Lake, 238 sites (many loops; loops A-G+M reservable, K/L FCFS), 51 lakeside sites, max RV 35 ft / trailer 30 ft, no hookups, flush toilets, boat ramps. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Sharps Creek Recreation Site
note: BLM (Northwest Oregon District) campground alongside Sharps Creek, 12 sites, no hookups, vault toilets and running water, swimming hole; sites accommodate RVs (roughly to 25-40 ft per sources). Open Memorial Day through early fall; half reservable online, half FCFS. --Claude

name: Eightmile Campground
note: Mt. Hood NF (Barlow Ranger District) campground along Eightmile Creek, 19 large sites, max vehicle 30 ft, vault toilets, no potable water. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Doe Point Campground
note: Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (High Cascades RD) drive-in campground in old-growth forest adjacent Fish Lake, ~35 sites (30 fit trailers/RVs, 5 tent-only), picnic table & fire ring per site, no hookups. Reservable online with some FCFS. --Claude

name: Dougherty Campground
note: Rustic Wallowa-Whitman NF (Hells Canyon NRA) campground in open pine/grassland near Billy Meadows: 12 sites (4 tent/trailer, 8 tent-only), vault toilet, no water, no hookups. Reached via ~40 mi of maintained gravel forest roads (FR 46) off Hwy 3 north of Enterprise. First-come, first-served, self-pay; season ~June-early Oct. --Claude

name: Irondyke Forest Camp
note: Primitive 5-site Wallowa-Whitman NF camp along the Wild & Scenic Lostine River (~5,200 ft), picnic table + fire ring, vault toilet, no potable water, no hookups. Accessed via Lostine River Road/FR 8210 (paved then rough, narrow, washboard gravel) - passable by smaller rigs (horse trailers use it) but tight for big RVs. First-come, first-served, self-pay; season ~June-Sept. --Claude

name: Lick Creek Campground
note: Wallowa-Whitman NF campground on the Hells Canyon Scenic Byway (FR 39) along Lick Creek: 9 sites, ~5 fit small/medium RVs, vault toilet, no hookups. First-come, first-served, self-pay kiosk; byway usually snow-free late May/June-Sept/Oct. --Claude

name: Olallie Meadow Campground
note: USFS (Mt. Hood NF) at ~4,500 ft beside Olallie Meadow, reached via ~3 mi of gravel (FR 4690) then FR 4220. 7-site first-come, first-served campground, max vehicle 24 ft, no hookups, open ~mid-June-mid-Sept (snow-gated). --Claude

name: Riverside Campground
note: 16 single-family sites (sites 1-4 walk-in) strung along the Oak Grove Fork of the Clackamas River in Mt. Hood NF, ~1,400 ft; max vehicle length ~24 ft; vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups. Mix of reservable (recreation.gov) and FCFS. --Claude

name: Puma Campground
note: Last developed campground on FR 18 in the Fall Creek corridor, Willamette NF, ~1,160 ft; 11 sites (3 tent-only), max RV ~25 ft; vault toilets, hand-pump water, no hookups. Reservable on recreation.gov plus some FCFS. In the 2023 Bedrock Fire burn (little remaining shade); Forest Service lists it open for the 2026 season. --Claude

name: Lockaby Campground
note: USFS (Mt. Hood NF, Clackamas River Ranger District). Small drive-in campground on the Wild & Scenic Clackamas River just upstream of Carter Bridge; heavily burned in the 2020 Riverside Fire but operating first-come, first-served in 2026. Max RV length not posted; drive-in tent/RV sites. --Claude

name: Ripplebrook Campground
note: USFS (Mt. Hood NF, Clackamas River Ranger District). Small (~13-site) drive-in campground along the Oak Grove Fork of the Clackamas River near the historic Ripplebrook junction; operating first-come, first-served in 2026, no hookups, tent/RV sites. Max RV length not posted. --Claude

name: Wolf Creek Campground
note: Umpqua NF (concessionaire-run), NOT BLM despite the RV Life dnr tag, along the Little River. 8 sites (5 fit RVs/trailers, 3 tent-only), max vehicle ~30 ft, potable water, no hookups. First-come, first-served (a separate reservable group site adjoins it). --Claude

name: North Arm Campground (Timothy Lake)
note: USFS (Mt. Hood NF) campground managed by Portland General Electric on Timothy Lake's northeast shore. 14 tent/RV sites, no hookups; RVs to 45 ft but the access road is rough. Reservable online (open reservable sites go FCFS for one night). --Claude

name: Trillium Lake Campground
note: Popular Mt. Hood NF campground on 63-acre Trillium Lake with a small boat ramp in the campground and classic Mt. Hood views. 57 sites (14 tent-only), no hookups, max vehicle length 40 ft. Mostly reservable online with some FCFS. --Claude

name: Olive Lake Campground
note: Umatilla NF campground on Olive Lake high in the Blue Mountains (~6,050 ft), reached by gravel forest road ~12 mi west of Granite. 20 tent/RV sites plus 6 tent-only and 2 group; no hookups and no potable water on site (water 7 mi away at Fremont Powerhouse). Most sites suit tents but some accommodate RVs. Some FCFS, some reservable. --Claude

name: Macks Canyon Recreation Site
note: BLM (Prineville District) campground at the end of the Lower Deschutes River Access Road, on the east bank of the lower Deschutes. 18 individual + 2 group sites, vault toilets, no water or hookups; big rigs fit but the gravel access road is washboard (drive ~20 mph). First-come, first-served, open year-round. --Claude

name: Yellowjacket Campground
note: Malheur NF (Emigrant Creek RD) campground on the shore of Yellowjacket Lake; ~20 open drive-in sites fitting trailers/RVs, vault toilets, hand-pump drinking water (seasonal). Reached by ~33 mi of paved/gravel forest roads from Burns. The surrounding forest burned in the 2024-25 Falls Fire and the campground was closed through 2025; the closure order expired at the end of 2025 (loop and lake intact on satellite) — verify open before a trip. Elev ~4840 ft. --Claude Rechecked 2026-09-30: closed under the Falls Fire area closure (recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Coalmine Hill Campground
note: Umatilla NF (Heppner RD) FCFS campground atop Coalmine Hill; one larger pull-in site near the entrance plus sites around a large parking area big enough to turn an RV or horse trailer, one vault toilet, a horse corral, and trailhead access to the Willow Creek/Bald Mountain/Hells Half Acre trails; no potable water or garbage service. Maintained Memorial Day to mid-November; ~22 mi from Heppner on County Road 678. Elev ~4850 ft. --Claude

name: Lost Lake Resort & Campground
note: Concessionaire-run campground on Mt. Hood NF land at Lost Lake, 25 mi SW of Hood River. 148 sites across multiple loops; some D-loop sites take RVs to 40 ft, ~64 sites fit 20+ ft rigs. Drinking water, some sewer hookups, boat launch, fishing dock. Reservable on recreation.gov (unreserved go FCFS); open late Apr-mid Oct. --Claude

name: Wyeth Campground
note: Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area (USFS) campground off I-84 exit 51 near Cascade Locks, set in Douglas-fir/bigleaf-maple forest along Gorton Creek. 13 single sites + 3 group sites; RVs/trailers under 30 ft. Potable water, flush toilet, no hookups. Sites 1-2 FCFS, rest reservable on recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Marion Forks Campground
note: Willamette NF (Detroit RD) campground on Hwy 22 by Marion Creek and the Marion Forks fish hatchery, 16 mi SE of Detroit. 15 sites (one pull-through), RVs/trailers to 24 ft; tables, vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Riverside at Detroit Campground
note: Willamette NF (Detroit RD) campground along the North Santiam River in the North Santiam corridor, ~14 mi SE of Detroit on Hwy 22. 32 single sites + 1 double in two loops, trailers to 24 ft; individual water risers, vault toilets, no hookups. Reservable on recreation.gov with FCFS sites. --Claude

name: Santiam Flats Campground
note: Willamette NF (Detroit RD) campground at the upper (North Santiam) end of Detroit Lake, ~2.6 mi E of Detroit off Hwy 22 at Blowout Rd/FR 10. 31 sites (26 single, 5 double), trailers to 30 ft; dry camping (no hookups), water spigots, vault toilets. Fully reservable on recreation.gov (FCFS only if unreserved). --Claude

name: Whispering Falls Campground
note: Willamette NF (Detroit RD) campground next to the North Santiam River in old-growth forest, North Santiam corridor. 16 sites with gravel spurs 30-40 ft (RVs to ~40 ft); drinking water, vault toilets, no hookups. 10 sites reservable on recreation.gov, rest FCFS; open ~May-Sep. --Claude

name: Bogus Creek Campground
note: Umpqua NF (North Umpqua RD) campground near the Wild & Scenic North Umpqua River in old-growth Douglas-fir, Hwy 138 corridor. 14-15 sites, RVs/trailers to 30 ft; paved roads and spurs, potable water, flush toilets, tables/fire rings. Reservable on recreation.gov (FCFS if unreserved). River access within walking distance. --Claude

name: Lake In The Woods Campground
note: Umpqua NF campground beside a small 4-acre man-made lake, reached via ~18 mi of one-lane gravel (FR 27) up the Little River. 11 sites, tents/trailers to 35 ft, vault toilets, no potable water/no hookups. First-come, first-served (Scan & Pay via recreation.gov app). Long gravel access, but drive-in. --Claude

name: Lone Pine Group Campground
note: BLM Roseburg District campground on a loop along Rock Creek (flows to North Umpqua), ~10 mi from Glide. Historically a group campground, now released for individual site rentals for the 2026 summer/fall season (11 sites, no drinking water). Reservation only on recreation.gov, no FCFS. RV Life 4.5*/$$$$ (auto 7/2026; $$$$ reflects legacy group-site pricing). --Claude
